scenario.name: r-cd-chained-depth-2
scenario.description: Depth-2 delegate chain: parent→child→grandchild→depth-1 recovery wake→root return→structured root consumption. The proven composition uses fanoutMode=tree, exactly two completed/delivered task rows, and a post-return root run that consumes both results.

invocation.promptTemplate: Proof chain nonce {{nonce}}: you are depth-1. First call continue_delegate(mode='silent-wake', fanoutMode='tree', task='Grandchild nonce {{nonce}}: reply exactly GRANDCHILD-DONE {{nonce}} only after you arrive. Do not mutate files.'). After that tool reports scheduled, call continue_work(reason='R-CD-CHAIN {{nonce}} wake depth1 after leaf return', delaySeconds=15). On this first turn reply exactly CHILD-WAITING {{nonce}} CHILD-DELEGATE-SCHEDULED CHILD-WAKE-SCHEDULED. On the continuation wake, inspect the completed child return. Only after it contains GRANDCHILD-DONE {{nonce}}, reply exactly CHILD-DONE {{nonce}} CHILD-SAW-GRANDCHILD. If the leaf is not complete, call continue_work once more with the same reason and do not emit CHILD-DONE.

expectedReceipts.name: child-spawns
expectedReceipts.description: The fully resolved root task binds one distinct depth-1 child and its first result contains strict CHILD-WAITING {{nonce}} CHILD-DELEGATE-SCHEDULED CHILD-WAKE-SCHEDULED

expectedReceipts.name: child-fires-grandchild
expectedReceipts.description: CHILD-WAITING sentinel confirms depth-1 scheduled both its nested continue_delegate and its post-leaf continue_work recovery wake

expectedReceipts.name: depth1-recovery-wake
expectedReceipts.description: Depth-1 wakes after the leaf, verifies GRANDCHILD-DONE, and only then emits CHILD-DONE CHILD-SAW-GRANDCHILD

expectedReceipts.name: grandchild-spawns
expectedReceipts.description: The fully resolved depth-1 task binds one distinct depth-2 grandchild

expectedReceipts.name: grandchild-returns
expectedReceipts.description: A nonce-bound grandchild identity and exact GRANDCHILD-DONE sentinel are observed after dispatch acceptance

expectedReceipts.name: exactly-once-chain-completion
expectedReceipts.description: A fully paginated tasks.list snapshot plus nonce-bound tasks.get details exposes exactly one root→child row and one child→grandchild row; both have unique task/run identities, status=completed, deliveryStatus=delivered, and depth exactly 2

expectedReceipts.name: root-consumes-chain-return
expectedReceipts.description: After both task rows complete, one root lifecycle run supplies the child marker in heartbeat_respond scratch and the grandchild marker in reason, receives status=accepted for that exact tool call, and ends successfully; ROOT-CHAIN-ACK {{nonce}} is supplemental only

expectedReceipts.name: r-cd-chained-depth-2-authoritative-receipt
expectedReceipts.description: HMAC-sealed public-safe row receipt binds candidate/runtime identity, exactly-once task completion, structured root consumption, and the typed-tool trace

expectedReceipts.name: trace-id
expectedReceipts.description: Trace ID for chain visualization in Tempo

review.notes: Depth-2 chain proof. PASS-candidate requires exactly two completed/delivered nonce-bound task rows and a later root lifecycle run whose structured heartbeat_respond input contains both return markers, whose exact tool call is accepted, and whose lifecycle ends successfully. ROOT-CHAIN-ACK is supplemental, never verdict authority.

census.limits: chain.id makes the chain itself partially rebindable, but each hop’s identity is not: no exported span says which run or turn was depth-1 versus depth-2, so a later reader can see that a chain existed and cannot reconstruct its shape or which seat produced it.

spans.name: continuation.delegate.dispatch
spans.notes: One per hop; hops are not distinguishable from each other in exported attributes.

attributes.notes: Emitted today and already asserted by the row’s trace-correlation resolver. It is the strongest join currently available and it is not an identity.
Hop depth on the accepted entry span. Without it a depth-2 chain and two unrelated depth-1 dispatches look alike.
Accepted entry spans carry no signal.kind on the census product basis; origin is contracted by R-OBS-CONT-PROVENANCE.
No k6/Project-81 resource or trace marker exists, so this row’s traffic cannot be separated from organic fleet traffic in a later census.

redaction.rule: Hop identities are published as nonce-bound fingerprints. Chain task text, heartbeat inputs, grandchild prompt bodies, raw session/task/run/tool-call keys, and tokens never enter the artifact.

controls.positive: Exactly two nonce-bound task rows form root→child→grandchild, both complete and deliver once, and a later root lifecycle run submits both markers through structured heartbeat_respond fields, receives status=accepted for the same tool-call id, and ends successfully.
controls.negative: Prompt echoes, phrase-only ROOT-CHAIN-ACK, descendant output, rejected or mismatched heartbeat calls, incomplete/duplicate task rows, and structured delivery without a later successful same-run lifecycle end never satisfy the receipt.
controls.notes: Depth is established by the task-ledger relationship and distinct identities; ROOT-CHAIN-ACK remains supplemental.

backendUnavailable.notes: A degraded backend removes chain visualization only. The behavioral receipts stand on the gateway event stream and the row stays PARTIAL for the missing trace.

verdictAuthority.pass: Exactly two completed/delivered task rows at depth 2 plus a later structured root heartbeat input, matching accepted tool result, and successful same-run lifecycle end. Behavioral only.
verdictAuthority.partial: A hop identity or the trace receipt is unavailable, or the telemetry backend is degraded or partial.
verdictAuthority.fail: The root lacks the structured post-return consumption boundary, either return is absent/duplicated, task/run identities or nonce do not bind, candidate identity differs, or depth is not exactly 2.

execution.deterministicK6: r-cd-chained-depth-2.js fires the exact committed manifest task; the row-scoped resolver signs the exactly-once task ledger and same-run root consumption receipt.
execution.manual: Per-seat cross-walk runs (TEST-1/2/3) remain manual and are filed under the row’s canonical path with their substitution recorded.
execution.relationship: The deterministic row is the verdict authority for chain shape; manual cross-walks add seat coverage and never substitute for a missing hop receipt.

liveRunSafety.notes: Live depth-2 chain row. Prefer OPENCLAW_CREATE_DISPOSABLE_SESSION=true. The depth-1 task must use fanoutMode=tree and a continue_work recovery wake; immediate return after scheduling is the committed negative control. Root return receives a fresh post-grandchild observation window. The signed structured receipt, not ROOT-CHAIN-ACK wording, owns the candidate verdict.
